taste_definition: Taste is the quality of a code artifact judged on its code, its communication, and its test writing — beyond whether it works. Judge taste only: never feature count, never mere correctness.

clarity.label: Clarity & structure
clarity.instructions: How clearly do `artifact`'s names, decomposition, and control flow convey what the code does and why? Judge the code in `artifact` against `task.brief`.
levels: Misleading — names or structure obscure or invert what the code does
Opaque — decipherable only by tracing execution line by line
Understandable — conventional layout and mostly clear names, with some puzzling spots
Clear — reads at the level of the idea; intent obvious from names and shape
Exemplary — the structure itself explains the domain; a newcomer learns the model from the code

idiom.label: Idiom & economy
idiom.instructions: How well does `artifact` use the language's idioms at the right size — no redundant machinery (thin wrappers, needless copies, hand-rolled library work, premature abstraction)?
levels: Fights the language — hand-rolls what the platform provides, or abuses its constructs
Wasteful — noticeable redundant machinery: thin wrappers, needless copies, abstraction that earns nothing
Competent — idiomatic baseline with a few needless parts
Lean — every construct earns its place; the deletion test passes
Fluent — the shortest clear form; idiomatic shortcuts used exactly where they help

signal.label: Signal discipline
signal.instructions: Do `artifact`'s comments and cosmetics carry signal? Narration comments, step banners, section dividers, restating comments, emoji, and tutorial voice are slop; why-comments, SAFETY notes, and invariant documentation are signal.
levels: Slop-saturated — narration, banners, emoji, or restating comments dominate
Noisy — regular slop tells (trivial comments, tutorial voice) with little signal
Mixed — uneven: some slop, some useful commentary
Quiet — comments only where they carry why, invariants, or hazards
Austere — nothing decorative; every comment is load-bearing

comms.label: Communication
comms.instructions: How well does `context.explanation` communicate — accurate, concise, honest about tradeoffs and limits? Confusing or padded explanation is poor taste even when the code is fine. Omitted when `has_explanation` is false.
levels: Misleading — contradicts or oversells the code
Confusing — verbose, hedging, or hard to follow
Serviceable — correct but padded or generic
Clear — concise, accurate, states what matters
Trusted — precise about tradeoffs and limits; you would forward it

tests.label: Test taste
tests.instructions: Do `artifact`'s tests earn their place — verify the real contract including failure paths, without scaffolding or mock theater? Missing tests where the task needs them is the floor. Omitted when `task.tests_expected` is false.
levels: Missing where the task needs them, or counterproductive — proves nothing or asserts mock echoes
Slop-heavy — verbose scaffolding, imprecise matchers, bleeding state
Present — checks something real but shallow or duplicative
Earned — verifies the actual contract including failure paths
Model — minimal, precise, and itself teaches the contract

has_explanation.instructions: `context.explanation` is present and substantive (not an empty string or a one-line stub).

type_laundering.instructions: `artifact` launders types: chained or `as any` assertions, widen-then-assert casts, or fabricated type evidence instead of validation.

unvalidated_boundary.instructions: `artifact` treats unvalidated boundary data (raw `JSON.parse` results, external input) as typed or trusted.

accumulating_copy.instructions: `artifact` grows collections by copying: accumulating spread in reducers/loops, `Object.assign({}, acc, …)`, `concat`/`slice` accumulator chains.

eager_pipeline.instructions: `artifact` allocates needless intermediates in pipelines, e.g. adjacent eager `.filter().map()` chains where one pass or a lazy pipeline fits.

comment_slop.instructions: `artifact` carries comment slop: narrative, trivial, step-banner, divider, or placeholder comments that restate or perform rather than explain.

emoji_marketing.instructions: `artifact` or its output strings use emoji narration or marketing tone.

inflated_prose.instructions: `artifact`'s comments or docs use inflated vocabulary or em-dash affectation instead of plain engineering language.

swallowed_errors.instructions: `artifact` swallows failures: empty or comment-only handlers, `except: pass`, catch-and-return-fallback that changes the failure path silently.

placeholder_residue.instructions: `artifact` leaves residue: orphan TODOs, empty functions, console leftovers, dead or unreachable code from discarded approaches.

ceremony_structure.instructions: `artifact` builds ceremony: thin wrappers, single-use helpers, static-only classes, factories for one use case — abstraction that deletes nothing.

self_proving_tests.instructions: `artifact`'s tests prove nothing: they mock the code's own internals, assert mock echoes, or only exercise the happy path while claiming coverage.

silencing_tells.instructions: `artifact` silences tooling instead of fixing defects: suppression comments, `@ts-nocheck`, constant-condition dead branches, or rewrites that clear a warning while preserving the defect.

duel_instructions: Two candidate implementations of the same task are shown as `candidate_a` and `candidate_b`. Which has better taste as defined here: clarity & structure, idiom & economy, signal discipline, communication (their accompanying explanation), and test taste. Judge taste only — never feature count, never mere correctness. Pick `candidate_a`, `candidate_b`, or `too_close_to_call` when their taste is indistinguishable.

duel_criteria.candidate_a: The candidate shown as `candidate_a` has better taste.
duel_criteria.candidate_b: The candidate shown as `candidate_b` has better taste.
duel_criteria.too_close_to_call: The two candidates' taste is indistinguishable.

notes.contested_patterns: Conditional empty-object spread, TODO severity, JSDoc density, and boundary widening are contested across rulebases (research/slop-patterns.md); they are judged through the level descriptions above and never auto-flagged.
notes.composite: composite = mean of available dimension scores on the 0..4 level scale (JEV returns the expected level index); publish as percentage = composite/4. Dimensions gated by has_explanation / task.tests_expected are excluded and the mean renormalizes.
